text:
maya: Quick heads up 1 staging run: enabling connector cache + prefetch causes client queue growth and streaming stalls.

sam: Repro steps?

maya: 1) connector_cache=true 2) prefetch_window=10 3) load test: `wrk -c50 -t4` against /v1/stream. After ~25s inflight climbs and streams block.

maya: Snippet: ```
WARN runtime inflight=192 waiting=640 kv_hits=8
ERROR runtime lease_timeout waiting on permit held by retry-path
```

tia: Suspect token refresh path doesn't release the client permit on 401 before retrying.

jordan: Could be TTL + eviction too. Default cache_ttl=5m keeps session state around for streaming.

ops-eli: Workaround: reduce connector_cache_ttl to 30s and ensure lease.release() in all code paths.

maya: I tried that locally: set ttl=30s and wrapped acquire/release in try/finally. Staging stayed stable under same load.

sam: Please open a small PR with the finally and a config flag for ttl. Add a unit test that simulates a 401 mid-stream and asserts permit is released.

maya: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/pull/1543 (WIP) 1 adds `connectorCache.ttl` and release guard.

devex-bot: Issue created #4820-client-cache-lease-leak assigned to jordan 1 https://issues.redwood.ai/4820

jordan: I'll add the test + a staging canary with ttl=15s and prefetch=5. Also add telemetry "permits_held_on_retry" counter.

sam: Also update devex doc blurb: recommended cache_ttl streaming=15-30s, rr=5m+.

maya: Thanks, will follow up in the issue with logs and perf dump. :thumbsup:
